title: Current Model Family Selection Matrix
summary: Use a dated library spanning hosted, downloadable, text, vision, audio, video, code, reasoning, and retrieval models to build a workload-specific shortlist instead of relying on product rank or memory.
prerequisites: A defined workload with quality, safety, latency, and cost targets
Access to current provider model and lifecycle documentation

sections.title: Use this dated library as discovery, not a ranking
paragraphs: This library is a source snapshot checked on 2026-09-19. It is not a latest-model claim, benchmark ranking, or recommendation. Model names, deployable identifiers, lifecycle states, hosted availability, data terms, and prices can change. Reopen the exact first-party page before a purchase or production decision.

Keep four concepts separate. A model family is a related group such as Qwen3 or Whisper. A concrete version is an artifact such as Qwen3-0.6B or Whisper turbo. A product or hosting service is an API, cloud surface, playground, or model hub through which an artifact may be accessed. A runtime is software such as Transformers, vLLM, SGLang, or Transformers.js that loads or serves a model. Availability in a consumer chat product does not prove API availability, and a downloadable model card does not prove that a particular cloud region hosts it.

Open weights means weights are available to download under stated terms. It is not automatically equivalent to open-source software, nor does it prove that training data, training code, or the complete production system is available. Verify the license and any use restrictions for the exact model, code, tokenizer, datasets, runtime, and deployment. A model license is not all-purpose legal, privacy, trademark, export-control, or regulatory permission.

Capabilities vary by exact version. Do not infer that every member of a family accepts every modality. In particular, Qwen3-0.6B, GLM-4.5, SmolLM2-135M-Instruct, DeepSeek-V3.2-Exp, and gpt-oss are documented here as text models, not as image or audio models. Llama 4 accepts text and images, but not audio or video according to its card. Nemotron-3-Nano-Omni-30B-A3B-Reasoning accepts video, audio, images, and English text but produces text. Whisper is a speech model, not a general chat model. BGE-M3 produces retrieval representations rather than conversational answers.

sections.title: Broad model family library by useful capability
paragraphs: Multimodal text and vision entry 1, Meta Llama: Llama 4 is a natively multimodal, autoregressive mixture-of-experts family with early fusion for text and image understanding. Llama 4 Scout (17Bx16E) has 17B activated and 109B total parameters across 16 experts; Llama 4 Maverick (17Bx128E) has 17B activated and 400B total parameters across 128 experts. Both accept multilingual text and images and output multilingual text and code. Scout has a 10M-token context and Maverick a 1M-token context. The 12 supported languages are Arabic, English, French, German, Hindi, Indonesian, Italian, Portuguese, Spanish, Tagalog, Thai, and Vietnamese. The card records an April 5, 2025 release and August 2024 knowledge cutoff. Scout is released as BF16 weights and is stated to fit one H100 GPU with on-the-fly int4 quantization. Maverick is released as BF16 and downloadable FP8 weights, with FP8 stated to fit one H100 DGX host, not one H100 GPU. Use is governed by the custom Llama 4 Community License Agreement. Latency, cost, target-runtime memory, and workload quality are UNKNOWN. Source: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/meta-llama/llama-models/main/models/llama4/MODEL_CARD.md, checked 2026-09-19.

Text, code, and reasoning entry 2, DeepSeek: DeepSeek-V3.2-Exp is an experimental text and reasoning version built on V3.1-Terminus. Its repository says it introduces DeepSeek Sparse Attention for long-context efficiency and provides public reasoning, coding, and agentic benchmark results. It can be run from downloadable weights using the supplied inference code, SGLang containers, or vLLM recipes. The repository and model weights state an MIT license. The README also records a 2025-11-17 correction to the demo's RoPE implementation, so evaluation must pin corrected code. Hardware capacity, application latency, operating cost, and quality on a learner's workload remain UNKNOWN. Source: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V3.2/main/README.md, checked 2026-09-19.

Text, code, and reasoning entry 3, Qwen: Qwen3 is the family and Qwen3-0.6B is the concrete causal language model examined here. It has 0.6B parameters, 28 layers, and a documented 32,768-token context. It switches between thinking and non-thinking behavior and is described for reasoning, mathematics, coding, multilingual text, dialogue, and tool integration. It is not documented on this card as accepting image or audio input. Deployment options named by the card include Transformers, SGLang, vLLM, Ollama, LMStudio, MLX-LM, llama.cpp, and KTransformers. The exact artifact states Apache-2.0. Local latency, memory in each runtime, and task quality are UNKNOWN until measured. Source: https://huggingface.co/Qwen/Qwen3-0.6B/raw/main/README.md, checked 2026-09-19.

Multimodal entry 4, Microsoft Phi: Phi is the family and Phi-4-multimodal-instruct is the examined version. It accepts text, image, and audio and generates text, with a stated 128K-token context. Its card lists general image understanding, OCR, chart and table understanding, speech recognition, speech translation, speech question answering, and speech summarization. Text supports the card's listed 22 or more languages, while vision is listed as English and audio as a smaller language subset, so modality support must not be generalized across languages. The card links Azure, Hugging Face, GitHub, and NVIDIA playgrounds, while Transformers is the library named in its metadata. The artifact states MIT. Production hardware, hosted data handling, latency, and workload quality are UNKNOWN. Source: https://huggingface.co/microsoft/Phi-4-multimodal-instruct/raw/main/README.md, checked 2026-09-19.

Text and vision entry 5, Mistral: Mistral-Small-3.2-24B-Instruct-2506 is a concrete 24B instruct version and a minor update of Mistral Small 3.1. Its card documents text, function calling, and vision evaluation on MMMU, MathVista, ChartQA, DocVQA, and AI2D. It recommends vLLM and also documents Transformers. The example server configuration accepts images, and the card states that bf16 or fp16 GPU use requires approximately 55 GB of GPU RAM. This is a source-specific hardware statement, not a universal requirement for every quantization or hosted service. The artifact states Apache-2.0. Application latency, operating cost, and workload quality are UNKNOWN. Source: https://huggingface.co/mistralai/Mistral-Small-3.2-24B-Instruct-2506/raw/main/README.md, checked 2026-09-19.

Text, code, and agentic entry 6, Z.ai GLM: GLM-4.5 and GLM-4.5-Air are mixture-of-experts text models. GLM-4.5 is documented as 355B total and 32B active parameters; GLM-4.5-Air is 106B total and 12B active. Both provide thinking and non-thinking modes and are described for reasoning, coding, agents, and tool use, not image or audio input. Options include the Z.ai API and local serving with Transformers, vLLM, or SGLang. The model card provides large H100 or H200 configurations and says full 128K context requires still larger configurations, making infrastructure validation a blocking step. The exact artifacts state MIT. Latency, cost, and local workload quality are UNKNOWN. Source: https://huggingface.co/zai-org/GLM-4.5/raw/main/README.md, checked 2026-09-19.

Omni-input entry 7, NVIDIA Nemotron: the exact version is Nemotron-3-Nano-Omni-30B-A3B-Reasoning. Its Mamba2-Transformer hybrid MoE combines a Nemotron 3 Nano base LLM labeled 30B A3B, a CRADIO v4-H vision encoder, and a Parakeet speech encoder. NVIDIA labels the complete multimodal model 31B A3B, so 30B describes the base LLM while 31B describes the full model rather than representing a contradiction. It accepts English-only text, JPEG or PNG RGB images, WAV or MP3 audio up to one hour at 8 kHz or higher, and MP4 video up to two minutes. It outputs text and supports JSON, tool calling, word-level transcription timestamps, and reasoning output. The card gives a context maximum up to 256K tokens and lists BF16, FP8, and NVFP4 variants plus vLLM, TensorRT-LLM, TensorRT Edge-LLM, llama.cpp, Ollama, and SGLang runtimes. Model use is governed by the NVIDIA Open Model Agreement, while the hosted trial service has separate API Trial Terms. Independent quality, memory, latency, throughput, and cost are UNKNOWN. Source: https://build.nvidia.com/nvidia/nemotron-3-nano-omni-30b-a3b-reasoning/modelcard, checked 2026-09-19.

Compact text entry 8, Hugging Face SmolLM: SmolLM2 is a compact text-model family with 135M, 360M, and 1.7B sizes. The examined SmolLM2-135M-Instruct artifact has 135M parameters and was trained on 2 trillion tokens. Its card describes text rewriting and summarization, primarily in English, and warns that output may be inaccurate, inconsistent, or biased. It demonstrates Transformers on CUDA or CPU, TRL CLI on CPU, and Transformers.js. The exact artifact states Apache-2.0. It is not documented as a vision or speech model. On-device feasibility is plausible from the supplied examples, but actual latency, memory, and acceptable quality on the target device are UNKNOWN. Source: https://huggingface.co/HuggingFaceTB/SmolLM2-135M-Instruct/raw/main/README.md, checked 2026-09-19.

Text, reasoning, and agentic entry 9, OpenAI gpt-oss: gpt-oss is an open-weight model family, separate from OpenAI's hosted API catalog. The exact releases are gpt-oss-120b, with 117B parameters and 5.1B active, and gpt-oss-20b, with 21B parameters and 3.6B active. They are text models for configurable reasoning, function calling, structured outputs, and agentic tasks. They require the harmony response format. The repository documents Transformers, vLLM, and reference PyTorch, Triton, and Metal implementations. MXFP4 weights allow the 120b model to run on a single 80 GB GPU and the 20b model within 16 GB of memory under the documented setup. The artifacts state Apache 2.0. Those memory statements do not establish throughput, end-to-end latency, cost, or task quality, which remain UNKNOWN. Source: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/openai/gpt-oss/main/README.md, checked 2026-09-19.

Speech entry 10, OpenAI Whisper: Whisper is a speech-recognition family for multilingual transcription, speech translation into English, and spoken-language identification. The documented versions are tiny at 39M parameters, base at 74M, small at 244M, medium at 769M, large at 1550M, and turbo at 809M. English-only variants exist for tiny through medium. Turbo is optimized for transcription and is explicitly not trained for translation, so a multilingual tiny, base, small, medium, or large model is required for translation. Installation uses openai-whisper and requires ffmpeg. Code and weights state MIT. The repository reports hardware-specific relative speeds, but this library records application speed as UNKNOWN because the target hardware and audio are unspecified. Source: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/openai/whisper/main/README.md, checked 2026-09-19.

Hosted text and image entry 11, Anthropic Claude: Claude is a hosted model family accessed through the Claude API. The checked catalog lists Claude Fable 5.1, Claude Opus 5, Claude Sonnet 5, and Claude Haiku 4.5. The page states that these versions support text and image input, text output, multilingual use, vision, and tools. It lists 1M-token contexts for Fable 5.1, Opus 5, and Sonnet 5, and 200K for Haiku 4.5. These claims apply to the named versions, not every historical Claude. This is a product and API catalog, not evidence that downloadable weights are available. Region, data handling, application latency, workload quality, and effective cost under the learner's traffic pattern remain UNKNOWN and must be checked at the deployment surface. Source: https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/about-claude/models/overview, checked 2026-09-19.

Hosted multimodal entry 12, Google Gemini: Gemini is a hosted family available through the Gemini API, with capabilities varying by endpoint. The checked catalog includes Gemini 3.8 Flash for text-oriented coding and agentic work, Gemini 3.8 Live for low-latency voice interaction, Gemini 3.8 Live Extended Thinking for voice interaction with additional reasoning, Gemini 3.5 Transcribe for speech-to-text, image-generation endpoints, and Gemini Omni Flash for video generation and editing with audio. These are distinct concrete products and endpoints, not one model that should be assumed to perform every modality. Several older or preview endpoints also appear in the catalog, so lifecycle state must be recorded. Exact context, regional availability, prices, application latency, and workload quality are UNKNOWN in this matrix unless reverified from the exact endpoint documentation. Source: https://ai.google.dev/gemini-api/docs/models, checked 2026-09-19.

Embedding and reranking entry 13, BAAI BGE: BGE-M3 is a 1024-dimensional multilingual retrieval model with a documented maximum sequence length of 8192 tokens. It supports dense, sparse, and multi-vector retrieval. Its card recommends hybrid retrieval followed by a separate reranking stage and links BGE reranker implementations, but BGE-M3 itself should not be mislabeled as a generative chat model or as the reranker. The supplied card states MIT and documents FlagEmbedding, sentence-transformers, and Hugging Face Transformers use. Retrieval recall, ranking quality, index size, latency, and cost on the target corpus are UNKNOWN. Source: https://huggingface.co/BAAI/bge-m3/raw/main/README.md, checked 2026-09-19.

sections.title: Llama 4 modality and deployment distinctions
paragraphs: Llama 4 supports image understanding, captioning, visual reasoning, and image question answering, but its text-and-image input and text-and-code output specification does not establish image, audio, or video generation. Meta reports image-understanding testing with up to five input images. More than five images requires additional application-specific testing rather than an assumption that the documented result extends without limit.

Scout's 10M-token and Maverick's 1M-token context limits do not prove that a selected runtime can process the full window on available hardware. Likewise, Scout's stated fit on one H100 with on-the-fly int4 quantization is different from distributing a pre-quantized checkpoint. Maverick's downloadable FP8 weights and stated fit on one H100 DGX host describe a larger host-level configuration, not a single H100 GPU.

A suitable evaluation request for Scout is: attach a labeled water-cycle diagram and ask, "Explain this diagram to a 12-year-old in Spanish. List each visible stage, distinguish what you can read from what you infer, and finish with three comprehension questions." This request matches documented image input and Spanish text output. It was not executed. Accuracy, curriculum fit, full-context quality, runtime memory, speed, and cost remain UNKNOWN.

sections.title: Nemotron 3 Nano Omni modality, reasoning, and deployment distinctions
paragraphs: The exact model accepts four input types but remains English-only: MP4 video, WAV or MP3 audio, JPEG or PNG RGB images, and text strings. Its output is text. Audio understanding does not prove speech generation, and image or video understanding does not prove image or video generation. Raw PDF is not a documented input format; NVIDIA's example first renders PDF pages as images.

For the documented OpenAI-compatible local serving example, reasoning is on when the request omits the relevant chat-template option. The model then emits a reasoning trace before the final answer in the message content. The reasoning trace and final answer are distinct portions of that text output and applications must decide whether traces should be parsed, stored, displayed, or suppressed. For that documented interface, setting "chat_template_kwargs": {"enable_thinking": false} disables reasoning for the request so only the final answer appears in content. This is an exact model and request option, not a universal API convention.

A suitable evaluation request is: attach an English MP4 recording of a short science demonstration with spoken narration and ask, "Create a timestamped transcript, summarize the procedure, list each visible safety step, and mark any claim you cannot verify from the audio or frames." It uses documented media understanding, timestamps, and text output. It was not executed. Temporal grounding, transcription accuracy, OCR quality, trace handling, inference memory, speed, and cost remain UNKNOWN.

sections.title: Hosted OpenAI GPT models: API models are not downloadable weights
paragraphs: This dated entry covers OpenAI models served through the OpenAI API, not a universal ranking. The catalog checked on 2026-09-19 lists GPT-6 Astra as a flagship for complex reasoning and coding, and lists GPT-5.6 Sol, GPT-5.6 Terra, and GPT-5.6 Luna as current featured examples for professional, balanced, and cost-sensitive workloads. Their exact catalog identifiers are `gpt-6-astra`, `gpt-5.6-sol`, `gpt-5.6-terra`, and `gpt-5.6-luna`. The same catalog identifies GPT-5, with model ID `gpt-5` and default snapshot `gpt-5-2025-08-07`, as a previous reasoning model for coding and agentic tasks. The catalog recommends GPT-6 Astra as the newer starting point, but that is not evidence of better results on every workload. Lifecycle and availability must be rechecked before deployment.

GPT-6 Astra accepts text and images and produces text. Its documented context window is 1,050,000 tokens, with maximum input of 922,000 tokens and maximum output of 128,000 tokens. Its knowledge cutoff is 2026-04-30, and its reasoning effort can be `low`, `medium`, `high`, `xhigh`, or `max`. It supports Chat Completions at `v1/chat/completions`, Responses at `v1/responses`, and Batch at `v1/batch`. GPT-5 accepts text and images and produces text, with a 400,000-token context window, maximum input of 272,000 tokens, maximum output of 128,000 tokens, and a 2024-09-30 knowledge cutoff. Its reasoning effort options are `minimal`, `low`, `medium`, and `high`; it supports the same three endpoint categories. Image input does not mean image generation, and text output does not mean speech output. The catalog separately lists audio endpoints and models such as GPT-Audio, GPT-4o Audio, GPT-Transcribe, GPT-4o Mini TTS, and Whisper, plus image-generation models such as GPT-Image-2. These are specialized products, not capabilities to assume for a general text-and-vision GPT.

These are hosted API services: the provider operates the model and the learner sends requests to an approved endpoint. They are therefore different from `gpt-oss-120b` and `gpt-oss-20b`, which the existing guide describes as downloadable open-weight text models, and from Whisper, which is a downloadable speech-recognition family. A hosted GPT page does not establish downloadable weights. For the exact hosted models in this entry, regional availability, data retention or training-use terms, contractual terms, and license details are UNKNOWN from the supplied model pages. Verify them at the intended deployment surface. Hardware requirements for the client are UNKNOWN, while provider-side hardware is managed by the service. Quality, latency, and effective cost for a real application are also UNKNOWN. Measure all three on the same representative workload, prompt, output limit, tools, traffic pattern, and failure policy before choosing.

A concrete starting hypothesis is to use GPT-6 Astra for a difficult document task requiring text and image understanding, or GPT-5 for a controlled comparison against a previous reasoning model. This is a hypothesis, not a performance claim. An unexecuted Responses API-shaped example is:

The request asks for faithful extraction and uncertainty marking, but no API call or result is claimed. For the fictional Cedar Clinic, hosted API use is forbidden until the clinic's privacy, security, procurement, and external-service approvals are complete, regardless of whether the brand is OpenAI, another provider, or a hosted version of an open-weight model.

Learner exercise: Cedar Clinic needs an on-premises English summary of a patient appointment transcript, has a 24 GB GPU, and is considering `gpt-oss-20b` versus GPT-6 Astra. Which is eligible now, and what evidence is missing? Explained answer: `gpt-oss-20b` is the conditional candidate because the existing guide documents downloadable weights and a documented MXFP4 setup within 16 GB of memory. That does not prove summary quality, latency, or safe handling. GPT-6 Astra is hosted, so it violates the clinic's current deployment rule until approval, even if it might be convenient or capable. The learner must not infer universal superiority from model labels. The clinic still needs a fixed evaluation set, privacy and license review, actual memory and latency measurements, quality checks for invented dates and medication names, and an operating-cost record. No winner can be selected from documentation alone.

sections.title: Choose a category before choosing a name
paragraphs: For text generation, summarization, extraction, or dialogue, begin with a text instruct model. The sourced candidates include Llama 4, Qwen3-0.6B, SmolLM2-135M-Instruct, Mistral-Small-3.2-24B-Instruct-2506, DeepSeek-V3.2-Exp, GLM-4.5, gpt-oss, Claude, Gemini, Phi-4-multimodal-instruct, and English-only Nemotron-3-Nano-Omni-30B-A3B-Reasoning. Their size, deployment model, language coverage, and instruction quality differ.

For code, multi-step reasoning, or tool use, require an exact version that documents those functions and test tool-call syntax and failure recovery. Llama 4, DeepSeek-V3.2-Exp, Qwen3-0.6B, GLM-4.5, gpt-oss, Claude, Gemini, Mistral Small 3.2, Phi-4-multimodal-instruct, and Nemotron provide relevant sourced claims. A reasoning or agentic label does not prove correctness, security, or reliable tool execution.

For image understanding, choose an image-input version such as Llama 4 Scout or Maverick, Nemotron-3-Nano-Omni-30B-A3B-Reasoning, Phi-4-multimodal-instruct, Mistral-Small-3.2-24B-Instruct-2506, a checked current Claude version, or a suitable Gemini endpoint. Image understanding is distinct from image generation. Do not place DeepSeek-V3.2-Exp, Qwen3-0.6B, GLM-4.5, SmolLM2-135M-Instruct, gpt-oss, Whisper, or BGE-M3 in an image-input shortlist based on the supplied evidence.

For speech and audio, distinguish transcription, translation, understanding, synthesis, and real-time conversation. Whisper supports transcription and translation into English, but Whisper turbo is not a translation model. Phi-4-multimodal-instruct accepts audio for several speech tasks. Nemotron accepts English audio and video and can return text and word-level timestamps, but its English-only limit excludes Spanish-input uses. Gemini exposes distinct Live, Transcribe, translation, and text-to-speech endpoints. None of these facts makes every family member interchangeable.

For semantic search or retrieval-augmented generation, use an embedding or retrieval model before a generator. BGE-M3 is the supplied exact embedding example. Measure retrieval recall and ranking quality separately from answer quality. The supplied source mentions separate BGE reranker families but does not establish one exact reranker artifact for this matrix. The gap task is to select an exact reranker repository and license, then evaluate it on labeled query-document pairs rather than inventing a model entry.

sections.title: Apply deployment, data, hardware, and evaluation constraints
paragraphs: Deployment choice changes the evidence required. A hosted API needs exact endpoint, lifecycle, region, data retention and training-use terms, access controls, quotas, outage handling, and current rates. Self-hosting needs weight provenance, license review, runtime and driver compatibility, quantization validation, memory capacity, observability, patching, scaling, and incident ownership. A playground is useful for discovery but is not production evidence.

Hardware fit cannot be inferred from parameter count alone. Precision, quantization, context length, cache size, concurrency, runtime kernels, modality encoders, and accelerator type affect memory and speed. Treat the supplied Llama, Nemotron, Mistral, GLM, Whisper, and gpt-oss hardware statements as configurations described by their sources, not guarantees for another system.

Latency and cost must be measured at the application boundary. Record time to first output, total response time, tail latency, failure and retry behavior, input and output usage, infrastructure utilization, and any retrieval or tool costs. The research set provides no comparable cross-model production latency or cost, so those values are UNKNOWN.

Quality evaluation must represent the task and its critical slices. Examples include medication names and accented speech for transcription, OCR on low-resolution forms for vision, compilable patches for code, correct citations for retrieval-grounded answers, and valid arguments plus safe retries for tools. Public benchmarks can support discovery, but they do not certify a model for the organization's prompts, users, data, or risk level.

Stop promotion if a required modality, language, region, license term, or data control is unverified; the model does not fit approved hardware; a critical case fails; comparison settings differ; a source is stale; reasoning traces are exposed contrary to policy; or the approved evaluation or spending boundary is exceeded.

sections.title: Worked constrained decision for a fictional organization
paragraphs: Scenario inputs: Cedar Clinic Cooperative is fictional. It needs private English and Spanish appointment-call transcription, English summaries of those transcripts, and semantic retrieval over 40,000 internal English policy paragraphs. Raw audio and transcripts may contain patient information and must remain on premises. The clinic has office CPUs and one server with a 24 GB GPU. It has no approved external AI API, no image task, and no need for speech synthesis. Operators require a fallback that preserves the original audio and transcript. Before production, the clinic requires at least 98 percent accuracy on a manually labeled set of critical medication names, no invented appointment dates in 100 critical summary cases, retrieval recall at 10 of at least 90 percent on 200 labeled policy questions, and measured end-to-end latency within its internally chosen service target. These are fictional organizational acceptance thresholds, not observed results.

First elimination: hosted Claude and Gemini endpoints are ineligible until an external service and its data terms are approved. This is a privacy and permission decision, not a claim that the services are insecure. Llama 4 is excluded from transcription because its card does not document audio input. Its text capability does not make it hardware-eligible for summaries: Scout's stated fit uses one H100 with on-the-fly int4, Maverick FP8 uses an H100 DGX host, and neither establishes fit on a 24 GB GPU. Nemotron is excluded from the bilingual transcription requirement because its documented input language is English only; its fit on the clinic's 24 GB GPU is also UNKNOWN. DeepSeek-V3.2-Exp and the GLM-4.5 variants are not shortlisted because fit on the available GPU is not established by the supplied configurations. Mistral-Small-3.2 in bf16 or fp16 is eliminated under the card's approximately 55 GB GPU-memory statement. Image-capable models receive no advantage because there is no image requirement.

Audio shortlist: multilingual Whisper small or medium are conditional candidates for English and Spanish transcription and translation into English. Whisper turbo is excluded from translation because its README says it is not trained for that task. Phi-4-multimodal-instruct is another conditional audio candidate, but its production hardware fit on 24 GB is UNKNOWN. The clinic must test native-language transcription, translated transcription, speaker overlap, noise, names, and timestamps if timestamps are required.

Summary shortlist: gpt-oss-20b is conditionally hardware-eligible because the documented MXFP4 setup fits within 16 GB, leaving validation necessary on the actual 24 GB server and required harmony format. Qwen3-0.6B and SmolLM2-135M-Instruct are local text candidates, with SmolLM2 offering an explicit CPU path. Their summary fidelity is UNKNOWN. Phi-4-multimodal-instruct could combine transcription and summarization only if hardware, accuracy, and operational behavior pass. Combining stages may simplify a pipeline, but it is not automatically more accurate or safer.

Retrieval shortlist: BGE-M3 is the sourced candidate because it supports dense, sparse, and multi-vector retrieval. Its 8192-token maximum does not imply that every policy paragraph should use that length. The clinic must version document segmentation, test recall at 10 on its 200 labeled questions, and decide whether a separately verified reranker is needed.

Conditional decision: run an unchanged local evaluation across Whisper small and medium for audio; SmolLM2-135M-Instruct, Qwen3-0.6B, and gpt-oss-20b for summaries where they fit; and BGE-M3 for retrieval. Include Phi-4-multimodal-instruct only after a memory probe shows that the approved configuration fits. Do not include English-only Nemotron in the bilingual audio gate, and do not assume Llama 4 fits the available GPU. No winner is certified because no execution results, latency measurements, or costs were supplied. Purchase or production approval requires measured evidence and license, security, and privacy review for each exact artifact and dependency.

code.label: Filled operational decision record, planned and not executed
code.code:
Task: Select local components for bilingual call transcription, English transcript summaries, and policy retrieval at fictional Cedar Clinic Cooperative.
Scope: On-premises processing only; English and Spanish audio; English summaries; 40,000 English policy paragraphs; office CPUs plus one 24 GB GPU; no image generation, speech synthesis, or external API.
Permissions: The clinic privacy owner may approve evaluation data; the ML lead may install reviewed artifacts in an isolated test environment; procurement may approve spending only after evaluation; operators may not upload patient data to an unapproved service.
Candidate: Whisper small or medium for audio; SmolLM2-135M-Instruct, Qwen3-0.6B, or gpt-oss-20b for summaries; BGE-M3 for retrieval; Phi-4-multimodal-instruct only after a memory probe.
Required capabilities: Local execution, English and Spanish transcription, translation into English when requested, faithful English summaries, retrieval over internal text, auditable artifact versions, and preservation of source audio and documents.
Evaluation: Manually label medication names; use 100 critical summary cases and 200 labeled retrieval questions; pin prompts, runtime, precision, decoding, hardware, and corpus; record critical-entity accuracy, invented dates, recall@10, latency distribution, memory, failures, and measured operating resources.
Observed tradeoffs: NOT RUN. Quality, latency, and operating cost are UNKNOWN. Source review alone is not execution evidence.
Stop conditions: Stop if data leaves the premises, an artifact or dependency lacks review, the model exceeds 24 GB GPU memory, the runtime changes between candidates, reasoning traces or protected data enter unauthorized logs, any critical safety threshold fails, the source becomes stale, or the authorized test boundary is exceeded.
Decision and expiry: HOLD pending measured evaluation. Owner: project42-editorial for this learning example; a real clinic must assign accountable technical, privacy, security, and procurement owners. Review date: 2026-10-19.
Verification: Hash and record downloaded artifacts; record exact runtime and configuration; repeat the unchanged evaluation; inspect slice-level errors; verify the call occurs through the real application boundary; obtain human privacy, security, license, and production approval.
Recovery: Route failed audio to human transcription or the last verified local model; retain the original audio and intermediate transcript; mark incomplete summaries; rebuild the prior verified retrieval index; reconcile queued work; and rerun the unchanged gate before promotion.

sections.title: Learner variation
paragraphs: Variation inputs: Pine Books is a fictional small retailer. It wants an English-only assistant that rewrites product descriptions and summarizes public supplier documents. Inputs contain no confidential or personal data. It must run on existing CPU-only laptops with no account or hosted API. There is no image, audio, retrieval, coding, or tool-use requirement. Commercial use must pass license review. The organization sets a three-second response target for a 150-word input and requires all quantities in the source to remain unchanged. No tests have been run.

Learner task: identify the required modality, eliminate clearly unsuitable entries, produce a conditional shortlist, list the missing evidence, and state whether a winner can be selected now. Then compare your response with the separate answer key.

sections.title: Explained answer key for the learner variation
paragraphs: Required category: English text-to-text instruction following. Image, audio, embedding, hosted-only, and large accelerator-dependent choices do not add required capability.

Conditional shortlist: SmolLM2-135M-Instruct is the strongest evidence-backed starting candidate because its card documents English text tasks and an explicit CPU command. Qwen3-0.6B may remain a second research candidate because its card names local runtimes, but CPU performance and memory on Pine Books' laptops are UNKNOWN. Its thinking mode may also be unnecessary for simple rewriting and should be controlled consistently during evaluation.

Eliminations: Whisper is an audio model; BGE-M3 is a retrieval model; hosted Claude and Gemini violate the no-account requirement; Mistral Small 3.2 has a supplied GPU configuration far beyond the stated environment; GLM and DeepSeek hardware fit is not established; gpt-oss-20b has a documented 16 GB memory configuration but not a supplied CPU-laptop performance result; Phi's extra modalities do not establish CPU fit. Llama 4 Scout's documented fit depends on one H100 with on-the-fly int4, while Maverick FP8 is documented for an H100 DGX host, so neither has evidence of CPU-laptop fit. Nemotron's listed deployment guidance targets NVIDIA GPU-accelerated systems and supplies no CPU-laptop fit result; its video, audio, and image inputs add no required capability here.

Missing evidence: exact laptop specifications, model and runtime versions, peak memory, three-second latency distribution, preservation of every source quantity, writing-quality rubric, failure rate, and legal review of the exact model plus dependencies. A winner cannot be selected before these tests.

Common mistake: choosing the model with the largest parameter count. Feedback: size does not prove CPU fit or quantity preservation. Common mistake: selecting a vision model because it is called multimodal. Feedback: extra modality is not useful when no image is supplied. Common mistake: treating Apache-2.0 or another model agreement as complete commercial approval. Feedback: review the exact artifact, dependencies, data, notices, agreement conditions, and applicable law. Common mistake: claiming that the three-second target is met from a model description. Feedback: the target is an acceptance criterion, and observed latency remains UNKNOWN until measured on the actual laptop.

sections.title: Hands-on no-account request-classification exercise
paragraphs: This paper exercise requires no account, download, model execution, or infrastructure. For each supplied request, classify the primary modality and output, identify an eligible model category, name evidence needed before deployment, and notice any category error.

Requests: A. "Turn this 12-page English policy into five bullet points." B. "Read the attached photograph of a damaged shipping label and extract the tracking number." C. "Transcribe this Spanish call and translate it into English." D. "Find the three internal policy passages most relevant to a refund question." E. "Generate a patch for this Python function and run the test tool." F. "Create spoken audio from this written announcement."

code.label: Exercise results and feedback
code.code:
A | Text input to text output | Text instruct model | Evaluate factual coverage, omitted exceptions, unsupported statements, context fit, latency, and cost. Feedback: an embedding model alone does not write the summary.
B | Image plus text instruction to text output | Vision-language model with image understanding or OCR evidence | Llama 4, Nemotron, Phi-4-multimodal-instruct, and Mistral Small 3.2 are sourced category examples; evaluate exact-character accuracy on damaged labels, unreadable-image handling, privacy, and human escalation. Feedback: do not select a text-only Qwen3-0.6B, GLM-4.5, SmolLM2, DeepSeek-V3.2-Exp, gpt-oss, Whisper, or BGE-M3 from this evidence set.
C | Audio input to text output, with translation | Multilingual speech model | Candidates can include a suitable multilingual Whisper size or Phi-4-multimodal-instruct; evaluate Spanish accents, noise, names, translation adequacy, timestamps if needed, latency, and local or hosted data handling. Feedback: Whisper turbo is not eligible for translation, and English-only Nemotron is not eligible for Spanish input.
D | Text query and corpus to ranked passages | Embedding/retrieval model, optionally followed by a separately verified reranker | BGE-M3 is the supplied exact retrieval example; evaluate recall@k, ranking metrics, language and document slices, index size, latency, and update behavior. Feedback: conversational fluency is not retrieval evidence.
E | Text/code input to code plus tool actions | Code-capable text model with documented tool use | Evaluate compilation, tests, security checks, tool-call validity, unauthorized actions, rollback, latency, and cost. Feedback: a reasoning label does not prove safe tool execution, and a displayed reasoning trace is not proof that the final answer or action is correct.
F | Text input to audio output | Speech-synthesis model or endpoint | The checked Gemini catalog lists distinct TTS endpoints; verify exact endpoint lifecycle, language, voice controls, safety, rights, latency, data terms, and rates. Feedback: Whisper transcribes audio, while Nemotron understands media and outputs text; neither is established here as a text-to-speech model.

sections.title: Expected result and verification
paragraphs: Expected result: a dated, conditional shortlist organized by required modality and deployment boundary, not a universal winner. Every retained candidate has an exact artifact or endpoint, a first-party source, a stated role in the system, and a list of unresolved evidence. UNKNOWN remains visible for unmeasured quality, latency, cost, and unsupported hardware claims.

Verification: reopen every cited first-party page on the decision date; confirm exact model or endpoint ID, lifecycle, modalities, context if required, language, region, data terms, license, runtime compatibility, reasoning-output behavior, and rates. Pin model artifacts, prompts, tools, retrieval state, decoding settings, hardware, and graders. Run the same representative cases through the real application boundary, record slice-level outcomes and failure modes, and obtain a human decision. Source review metadata does not mean a benchmark, installation, API call, or production test was executed.

Recovery: keep the last verified model, runtime, prompt, index, and configuration available. If a critical failure, stale source, lifecycle change, unacceptable data term, capacity problem, unauthorized trace exposure, or budget breach occurs, stop promotion; route to the verified fallback or human process; preserve inputs and intermediate state where authorized; reconcile partial tool or conversation state; and rerun the unchanged gate before a new promotion.

Review ownership and cadence: project42-editorial owns this learning resource and reviews it every 30 days. A deploying organization must separately assign owners for model risk, security, privacy, licensing, operations, evaluation, and purchasing.
